gaps.sentence: The roads were almost empty — the traffic was surprisingly ___.
gaps.explanation: light traffic means few vehicles on the road; its opposite is heavy traffic.

gaps.sentence: He ___ a speech at the wedding that moved everyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Make a speech' is the collocation; say/tell take different structures.

gaps.sentence: There was ___ fog at the airport all morning.
gaps.explanation: thick fog (or dense fog) is the standard collocation; 'strong fog' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: The manager ___ an announcement about the changes yesterday.
gaps.explanation: make an announcement is the fixed collocation for stating something publicly.

gaps.sentence: The ___ traffic added an hour to our journey.
gaps.explanation: heavy traffic means a lot of vehicles on the road; 'thick traffic' is not standard.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ great progress since she changed schools.
gaps.explanation: make progress is the collocation; after 'has' the past participle 'made' is needed.

gaps.sentence: Who will ___ responsibility for the project now that Jane has left?
gaps.explanation: take responsibility for something means to accept the duty of dealing with it.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.
